Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the reranker evaluation: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: improve SERP relevance for product search (reduce incorrect top-1s), measured by NDCG/MRR.
- Dataset: ~200k product records; team can provide a labeled eval set (~1k queries with relevance judgments) or we can help bootstrap.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 150ms for rerank path; throughput target ~200 qps in steady state.
- Desired pipeline: vector retrieval candidate generation + learned reranker for final ranking (hybrid approach).

Action items / next steps
1) We attached a reranker_eval_template.xlsx — please populate a sample of ~200 labeled queries (or share existing CSV) so our SEs can run an initial evaluation.
2) Please send any hard requirements (security/auth: API key vs mTLS, VPC/Private deployment) — we noted you asked about VPC/private.
3) Dev deep-dive: propose a 60-min technical session next week to walk through our ranking API, SDK examples, and a candidate tuning plan (Dev Patel to lead).

Technical clarifications we plan to cover in the deep-dive:
- SDK setup and authentication options (API key vs mTLS for Private)
- Routing/region and model selection to meet latency SLOs
- Candidate generation strategy (vector DB top_k) vs reranker top_n and recommended defaults
- Structured output from reranker (scores, explainability fields) and how to integrate tool-calling or downstream filters
- Evaluation metrics & recommended sweep ranges for top_k/top_n

Attachments: reranker_eval_template.xlsx, redwood_ranking_api_reference.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the sample set so we can run evaluations.

On Wed, Jun 10, 2026 at 2:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can keep momentum on the reranker evaluation: 

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for the notes. I wanted to answer your specific questions and add suggested defaults you can try in the initial eval.

1) Endpoint / SDK call
- We expose a dedicated ranking API separate from embeddings. Typical flow: 1) Vector DB returns candidate IDs (top_k_candidates) 2) POST /v1/rank (or via SDK: redwood.rerank.rank(candidates, query, model=..., options=...)) which returns a scored list and optional structured fields.
- SDK quickstart (python):
  pip install redwood-sdk
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")
  resp = client.rerank.rank(query="best running shoes for trail", candidates=candidate_list, model="reranker-v1", top_n=10)

2) Auth & security
- Hosted: API key in Authorization header (Bearer token).
- Dedicated/Private: support for mTLS and customer-managed keys; we can switch the call to a private endpoint in your VPC. We'll coordinate with your infra team if you need mTLS.

3) Candidate generation / top_k tradeoffs
- Recommendation: for product search, start with vector DB top_k_candidates in {50, 100, 200} and reranker_top_n in {5, 10, 20}.
- Tradeoffs: larger top_k increases recall (likelier the true relevant doc is included) but increases latency and compute for reranker. A two-stage approach (vector search -> reranker) is standard because rerankers are heavier but more accurate.

4) Latency guidance
- Empirically: with small models and optimized batch sizes, top_k_candidates=200 + rerank_top_n=10 can be in the 120–180ms P95 range on a dedicated low-latency path (depending on payload size and batch). If you need consistent sub-150ms P95 at production qps, we recommend:
  - Pre-filtering to reduce candidate size (category filters)
  - Using top_k_candidates=100 in steady-state and 200 for offline re-ranking experiments
  - Enabling caching for frequent queries and prefix KV cache for session-based requests

5) Evaluation metrics & tuning plan
- Metrics: NDCG@10 (primary), MRR@10, Precision@1, Recall@K for candidate generator.
- Suggested experiment grid: top_k_candidates {50,100,200}, reranker_top_n {5,10,20}. Compute NDCG@10 and MRR across the eval set and plot latency vs NDCG to find the knee.
- Dataset size: run initial runs on 1k labeled queries; if labels are costly, 200–500 well-curated queries can give directional signal.

6) Cost consideration
- Hybrid (retrieve+rerank) costs more per query than embedding-only but gives better precision at top ranks. We'll share estimated token/compute costs after we see expected top_n and qps.

7) Structured output / tooling
- The reranker returns an array of objects {id, score, explain: optional string, attributes: {...}} so it's straightforward to attach structured signals to downstream ranking or business rules. Tool calling (if you want to call external filters or enrichment services) can be wired in the rerank pipeline.

Next steps:
- If you can share a sample CSV using the attached template, I'll queue an initial evaluation run (expected turnaround 48–72 hours).
- Schedule the deep-dive — Tue 6/16 10:00 PDT works for me.
